title: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 463 (Power of court to grant relief in certain cases)

content.overview: If in a proceeding for negligence, default, breach of duty or breach of trust it appears that the officer acted honestly and reasonably, and that having regard to the circumstances he ought fairly to be excused, the court may relieve him.
content.glance: If in a proceeding for negligence, default, breach of duty or breach of trust it appears that the officer acted honestly and reasonably, and that having regard to the circumstances he ought fairly to be excused, the court may relieve him.
content.study: Companies Act, 2013 — Section 463 (Power of court to grant relief in certain cases). If in a proceeding for negligence, default, breach of duty or breach of trust it appears that the officer acted honestly and reasonably, and that having regard to the circumstances he ought fairly to be excused, the court may relieve him. Apply only the conditions, approvals, filings and penalties stated in the section. A rule made under the Act cannot contradict the section. Not a verified closure.

sections.heading: Rule
sections.body: If in a proceeding for negligence, default, breach of duty or breach of trust it appears that the officer acted honestly and reasonably, and that having regard to the circumstances he ought fairly to be excused, the court may relieve him.

sections.heading: Explanation
sections.body: Honesty and reasonableness are both required. Relief is discretionary. It is not a defence to fraud.
